## Collection & Soft-Brand Options for Hotel Conversions in Mexico


Soft brands are a hybrid between independent and core-branded properties. In general, soft-branded hotels enjoy the benefits of marketing programs and reservation systems of core brands, but have greater flexibility regarding facilities, services, and operating standards. They are frequently the choice of owners of hotels that have a historical reputation and identity of their own.


When an owner in Mexico is exploring collection or soft-brand conversion options, the following brands are most commonly considered:

---

### 🏨 Marriott International

Marriott played a pivotal role in expanding the soft brand hotel concept through its **Autograph Collection**, launched in 2010. Building on this success, Marriott expanded its offerings through the acquisition of Starwood Hotels and Resorts, adding other soft brands like **The Luxury Collection**, **Tribute Portfolio**, and **Design Hotels**.



**City Express by Marriott** — which was originally a lodging brand in Mexico before its acquisition by Marriott International — became a lower-end conversion brand for the multinational lodging company.


---

### 🏨 IHG Hotels & Resorts
IHG is one of the most active players in Mexico specifically for conversions. 
IHG's priority is Mexico — that's where the company sees the most opportunities and may generate 50% of its growth.


- **Vignette Collection (luxury/lifestyle):** 
IHG's soft brands include **Vignette Collection** (in the luxury and lifestyle segment) and **voco hotels** (in the premium segment), which enjoyed record opening and signing totals in 2024.
 
IHG signed two Vignette Collection properties in the Caribbean and Latin America region recently, along with opening one in Peru.


- **voco hotels (premium/upscale):** 
Six hotels in Mexico converted to IHG's upscale **voco** brand, growing voco's Mexico portfolio to 10 properties, in a deal with owner Alliance Hotels.
 
The hotels are in Cancún, Guadalajara, Ciudad Juárez, San Luis Potosí, Torreón, and Nuevo Laredo.


- **Garner (midscale):** 
Within two years of its August 2023 launch, the midscale conversion brand **Garner hotels** surpassed 120 open and pipeline hotels, gaining popularity with owners thanks to its competitive conversion cost per key, flexible design standards, and reduced pre-opening costs through a rapid conversion process.


---

### 🏨 Hilton

Hilton's soft brand collections include the **Curio Collection** and the **Tapestry Collection**.
 Both are designed to allow independent hotels to retain their unique identity while accessing Hilton's global distribution network.


**Spark by Hilton** is also positioned as a conversion-friendly brand, presenting the opportunity for owners of lower-end hotel properties to convert to the minimum standards of a Hilton brand.


---

### 🏨 Hyatt

**Unscripted by Hyatt**, positioned in the upscale segment, is designed to unlock growth through adaptive reuse and conversion-friendly opportunities. It gives independent properties and small portfolios a light-touch operating model and flexible brand standards — empowering owners to maintain their unique identity while benefiting from Hyatt's scale.



Hyatt also offers **The Unbound Collection** as a soft brand option.



**Alila** (by Hyatt) is also entering Latin America, with Alila Mayakoba rebranding from Andaz Mayakoba, marking the debut of the Alila brand in the region.


---

### 🏨 Wyndham

In Mexico City, soft brands such as the **Trademark Collection by Wyndham** and the **Registry Collection** can help reposition legacy assets into higher-yielding segments without heavy structural changes. When combined, these platforms allow operators to tailor service levels to local Mexican expectations while maintaining global consistency.



The Registry Collection and similar soft brand platforms allow owners to retain a distinctive Mexican identity while accessing global distribution — particularly relevant in secondary markets and Pueblos Mágicos, where cultural authenticity is a core part of the value proposition.


---

### 🏨 Choice Hotels

Choice Hotels International announced its **Ascend Hotel Collection** in 2008
, which remains one of the most established soft-brand collection platforms available to independent hotel owners looking for conversion with flexibility.

---

### 🏨 Accor

Accor's soft brand collection options include the **MGallery Hotel Collection** (upper upscale), **Emblems Collection** (luxury), and the more recently launched **Handwritten Collection** (midscale), broadening Accor's unrivaled brand portfolio across different segments.


---

### 🏨 Preferred Hotels & Resorts / Independent Collections

**Preferred Hotels & Resorts** is also active in Mexico, with boutique properties like the Volga in Mexico City's Colonia Cuauhtémoc operating as part of the Preferred Hotels & Resorts collection.


---

### Summary Table

| Brand Family | Soft Brand / Collection | Segment |
|---|---|---|
| Marriott | Autograph Collection, Luxury Collection, Tribute Portfolio, Design Hotels, City Express | Midscale–Luxury |
| IHG | Vignette Collection, voco, Garner | Midscale–Luxury |
| Hilton | Curio Collection, Tapestry Collection, Spark | Select–Upscale |
| Hyatt | Unscripted by Hyatt, The Unbound Collection | Upscale |
| Wyndham | Trademark Collection, Registry Collection | Upscale–Luxury |
| Choice Hotels | Ascend Hotel Collection | Midscale–Upscale |
| Accor | MGallery, Emblems Collection, Handwritten Collection | Midscale–Luxury |
| Independent | Preferred Hotels & Resorts, Hamak Hotels | Boutique/Luxury |

The right choice depends on the property's location, segment, size, and the owner's priorities — whether that's maximizing loyalty program exposure, minimizing renovation requirements, or preserving a unique local identity.
